about: Best-practice rules (AMPRS + cost). Each rule: pillar, level (required / recommended / consider), the guided step it belongs to, input "customer" when only the customer can supply what it checks (the easy button never fills those), why, the risk if it isn't followed, and its source. The check for each rule is in studio/src/rules.ts, by id.

rules.title: Edge clusters have two or more nodes
rules.why: Edge nodes carry north/south traffic and centralized services; two or more keep them running through a node failure.
rules.risk: A single edge node is a single point of failure for north/south traffic and centralized services.

rules.title: Tier-0 gateway active/active
rules.why: Active/active spreads north/south traffic over up to 8 edge nodes. Only active/standby supports stateful services on the Tier-0.
rules.risk: An active/standby Tier-0 runs on 2 edge nodes and doesn't scale out north/south traffic.

rules.title: Transit gateway active/standby with VCF Automation or vSphere Supervisor
rules.why: Broadcom requires an active/standby transit gateway for VCF Automation All Apps orgs and vSphere Supervisor.
rules.risk: VCF Automation All Apps orgs or vSphere Supervisor won't be supported on an active/active transit gateway.

rules.title: BFD between the Tier-0 and the physical switches
rules.why: BFD detects link failures quickly; BGP keeps its default timers (60/180 seconds).
rules.risk: Without BFD, a failed link is detected by the BGP hold timer, up to 180 seconds.

rules.title: Identity Broker in instance mode
rules.why: Instance mode is recommended for production; embedded mode is intended for labs and proofs of concept.
rules.risk: Embedded mode is intended for labs and proofs of concept, not production.

rules.title: Clusters keep capacity for one host failure
rules.why: vSphere HA admission control for one host failure, with percentage-based failover capacity.
rules.risk: After a host failure there may not be enough capacity to restart every VM.

rules.title: Fleet management deployed highly available
rules.why: The high-availability model runs three VCF Operations and three VCF Automation nodes, so fleet management keeps working through a node failure. Broadcom recommends it for production.
rules.risk: With the Simple model, one node failure takes VCF Operations or VCF Automation offline until it's restored.
rules.source: Planning a successful VCF 9.0 deployment (VMware Cloud Foundation blog)

rules.title: vSAN clusters start at four hosts
rules.why: With four or more hosts, vSAN rebuilds objects automatically after a host failure or during maintenance.
rules.risk: With three hosts, vSAN can't rebuild data after a host failure or during maintenance; data runs unprotected until the host returns.

rules.title: vSAN reserved capacity (host rebuild reserve) on
rules.why: Reserved capacity keeps operations and host-rebuild space free. Not supported on 3-node or stretched clusters.
rules.risk: After a host failure there may not be enough free capacity to rebuild its data.

rules.title: Break-glass accounts held and rotated
rules.why: Local administrator accounts still work when the identity provider is down: name who holds them and how often they're rotated.
rules.risk: Without a defined holder and rotation, admin access during an identity outage is unplanned.

rules.title: MTU 9000 for vMotion, vSAN and host TEPs
rules.why: Broadcom recommends 9000 for vMotion, vSAN and host TEPs, and on the distributed switch.
rules.risk: A smaller MTU lowers vMotion, vSAN and overlay throughput.

rules.title: Edge nodes large or extra large
rules.why: Large or extra large edge VMs (or bare metal) for throughput and services.
rules.risk: Small or medium edge nodes limit north/south throughput and services.

rules.title: DNS domain, DNS and NTP servers defined
rules.why: Every VCF component needs forward and reverse DNS; components need a common time source.
rules.risk: Deployment can't complete without DNS records and time sync.

rules.title: IP plan without conflicts
rules.why: Subnets don't overlap each other or reserved ranges; one VLAN per subnet; valid gateways; each subnet holds its addresses.
rules.risk: Overlapping, duplicate or undersized networks break routing or the deployment.

rules.title: Subnets with room to grow
rules.why: VCF can't change an infrastructure subnet's mask later, so size subnets for expansion.
rules.risk: Growth beyond a subnet needs a new network, because its mask can't be changed.

rules.title: Separate TEP VLANs for edges and hosts
rules.why: Separate edge and host TEP VLANs keep the two kinds of overlay traffic apart.
rules.risk: Edge and host TEP traffic share one VLAN and subnet.

rules.title: Host management and management VMs on their own VLANs
rules.why: Keeps ESX host management apart from the management appliances. Broadcom's default shares them; a dedicated network is a supported option.
rules.risk: Host management and the management VMs share one VLAN.

rules.title: Identity provider, provisioning and role matrix defined
rules.why: Access to VCF comes through one identity provider per broker, with groups mapped to roles.
rules.risk: Who can access what isn't designed.

rules.title: A unique private BGP ASN for each Tier-0
rules.why: Use a unique private BGP ASN for the Tier-0 gateway.
rules.risk: A public or reused ASN can leak or clash with routes elsewhere.

rules.title: No hosts set well beyond what a cluster needs
rules.why: A cluster whose host count is set by hand well above what it needs pays for unused cores.
rules.risk: Licensing and hardware for hosts the workload doesn't need.

rules.title: Memory tiering on memory-bound clusters
rules.why: On a cluster sized by memory, NVMe memory tiering can cut the host count.
rules.risk: More hosts (and licensed cores) than a memory-tiered cluster would need.

rules.title: CPUs have 16 or more cores
rules.why: VCF is licensed per core with a minimum of 16 cores per CPU, so a CPU with fewer cores costs as much to license as a 16-core one.
rules.risk: Hosts with CPUs under 16 cores pay for licensed cores they don't have.
rules.source: Broadcom KB 313548: Counting cores for VMware Cloud Foundation
